{{short description|Geometric theorem relating a given triangle and three angles to a point}}
[[File:GeneralisationOfNapoleonPoint.svg|300px|right|thumb|Adjacent colored angles are equal in measure. The point {{mvar|N}} is the Jacobi point for  triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} and these angles.]]

In [[plane geometry]], a '''Jacobi point''' is a point in the [[Euclidean plane]] determined by a [[triangle]] {{math|△''ABC''}} and a triple of angles {{mvar|&alpha;, &beta;, &gamma;}}. This information is sufficient to determine three points {{mvar|X, Y, Z}} such that 
<math display=block>\begin{align}
\angle ZAB &= \angle YAC &= \alpha, \\
\angle XBC &= \angle ZBA &= \beta, \\
\angle YCA &= \angle XCB &= \gamma. 
\end{align}</math>
Then, by a theorem of {{Interlanguage link|Karl Friedrich Andreas Jacobi|de}}, the lines {{mvar|AX, BY, CZ}} are [[concurrent lines|concurrent]],<ref name=Michael>{{cite book|first=Michael |last=de Villiers|title=Some Adventures in Euclidean Geometry|year=2009|publisher=Dynamic Mathematics Learning|isbn=9780557102952|pages=138–140}}</ref><ref>Glenn T. Vickers, "Reciprocal Jacobi Triangles and the McCay Cubic", ''Forum Geometricorum 15'', 2015, 179–183. http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2015volume15/FG201518.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180424052323/http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2015volume15/FG201518.pdf |date=2018-04-24 }}</ref><ref name=Vickers2016>Glenn T. Vickers, "The 19 Congruent Jacobi Triangles", ''[[Forum Geometricorum]]'' 16, 2016, 339–344. http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2016volume16/FG201642.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180424054006/http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2016volume16/FG201642.pdf |date=2018-04-24 }}</ref> at a point {{mvar|N}} called the Jacobi point.<ref name=Vickers2016/>

The Jacobi point is a generalization of the [[Fermat point]], which is obtained by letting {{math|1=''&alpha;'' = ''&beta;'' = ''&gamma;'' = 60°}} and {{math|△''ABC''}} having no angle being greater or equal to 120°.

If the three angles above are equal, then {{mvar|N}} lies on the [[rectangular hyperbola]] given in [[areal coordinates]] by

<math display=block>yz(\cot B - \cot C) + zx(\cot C - \cot A) + xy(\cot A - \cot B) = 0,</math>

which is [[Kiepert's hyperbola]]. Each choice of three equal angles determines a [[triangle center]].

The Jacobi point can be further generalized as follows:
If points ''K'', ''L'', ''M'', ''N'', ''O'' and ''P'' are constructed on the sides of triangle ''ABC'' so that ''BK/KC = CL/LB = CM/MA = AN/NC = AO/OB = BP/PA'', triangles ''OPD'', ''KLE'' and ''MNF'' are constructed so that ∠''DOP'' = ∠''FNM'', ∠''DPO'' = ∠''EKL'', ∠''ELK'' = ∠''FMN'' and triangles ''LMY'', ''NOZ'' and ''PKX'' are respectively similar to triangles ''OPD'', ''KLE'' and ''MNF'', then ''DY'', ''EZ'' and ''FX'' are concurrent.<ref>Michael de Villiers, "A further generalization of the Fermat-Torricelli point", ''Mathematical Gazette'', 1999, 14–16. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/270309612_8306_A_Further_Generalisation_of_the_Fermat-Torricelli_Point</ref>
